## Nieuw Amsterdam in Suriname: fort, museum, and the meeting of two rivers

Nieuw Amsterdam is a town in northeastern Suriname where the Commewijne River flows into the [Suriname River](/suriname/place/suriname-river/). It is home to the historic Fort Nieuw Amsterdam, surrounded by green riverbanks and river routes. The town brings together colonial military history and the everyday life of today's coastal region.

Travelers come from [Paramaribo](/suriname/place/paramaribo/) for another perspective on Suriname. In the capital, they see the historic streets and buildings; in Nieuw Amsterdam, they discover how the colony's river and sea approaches were defended.

## Why was the fort built here?

The confluence of the Suriname and Commewijne rivers was strategically important. Ships arriving by water passed the defensive position, with the colony's plantations and settlements lying beyond it. Construction of the fort began in 1734 and the main work was completed by 1747.

Built in the colonial period, the fort's construction and operation cannot be separated from forced labor and the plantation system. It later served other purposes: part of the site was used as a prison, and in the 20th century defensive positions became important again. These changes explain why traces of several historical eras coexist here.

Today the fort serves as an open-air museum and a site for historical exhibitions. It is the area's principal attraction, although the town and its landing stage also offer interesting river views.

## What to see in Nieuw Amsterdam

### Defensive ramparts and old structures

Earthen ramparts and various historic features survive within the fort. A walk through the grounds helps visitors imagine how the fortified position operated at the confluence. Remains of military buildings, artillery, and former service areas are especially interesting.

The museum introduces the history of the colony and its difficult legacy. Allow enough time for the exhibitions rather than looking only at the cannons: they date from different periods and are difficult to place in context without explanation.

### Museum and 20th-century history

Historical exhibitions are held on the fort grounds. One theme concerns the writer and anti-colonial thinker Anton de Kom. In March 2025, an exhibition devoted to him opened here in cooperation with the Netherlands Open Air Museum.

Exhibition content, opening hours, and access to individual rooms can change. Check current arrangements before traveling. Permanent collections and temporary exhibitions provide different reasons to visit, so specify the subject that interests you when arranging an excursion.

### The river landing and Commewijne scenery

The meeting of the rivers is worth seeing in its own right. The broad waters, green banks, and boat traffic are easy to appreciate. On an excursion from Paramaribo, Nieuw Amsterdam may serve as the boarding point for a boat even when a full visit to the fort is not included.

This distinction matters. An itinerary may say "arrival at Nieuw Amsterdam landing" without promising a museum visit. If the history of the fort interests you, make sure its exploration is explicitly included in the program.

## Getting here from Paramaribo

Road connections between the capital and Commewijne run across the Jules Albert Wijdenbosch Bridge. River excursions by boat are another option, revealing riverbanks, settlements, and the confluence from the water.

The better choice depends on your goals. A detailed museum visit needs sufficient time on land. A boat excursion offers more of the river, but its duration depends on the landing stage, weather, and agreed route.

Nieuw Amsterdam can be combined with [Peperpot Nature Park](/suriname/place/peperpot-nature-park/), where a former plantation has gradually become a green natural area. These are distinct stops: the fort focuses on military and colonial history, while Peperpot offers walks through vegetation and opportunities to observe nature.

## Nieuw Amsterdam on current Ada Tours itineraries

Our ["Guianas Adventure" tour](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/) includes an excursion around Paramaribo, a visit to Peperpot, arrival at the Nieuw Amsterdam landing, and a boat journey back into the city. Wildlife can sometimes be spotted on the river, but dolphin sightings are not guaranteed. Importantly, this program confirms the landing stage and boat transfer; a guided visit inside the fort should not be considered included unless specifically stated.

Nieuw Amsterdam also features in the Suriname portion of our ["Suriname, Guyana, and French Guiana" itinerary](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/). When choosing between tours, consider how much time is devoted to the fort itself compared with other countries and natural attractions.

History enthusiasts should compare the fort with [Jodensavanne](/suriname/place/jodensavanne/). Nieuw Amsterdam tells the story of the colony's river defenses and the fort's later roles; Jodensavanne explores a Sephardic community, its archaeological remains, and plantation society. Both reveal different dimensions of Suriname's past.

## Planning your visit

For a walk around the outdoor grounds, bring comfortable shoes, drinking water, and protection from sun and rain. The riverside is humid, and paths and museum areas may be uneven. If traveling by boat, pack items so they can be protected from splashes.

If you want to see a particular exhibition, check the museum's current schedule. On days involving a boat trip, agree on embarkation times and the order of stops: visiting Nieuw Amsterdam as a river port and visiting it as a history museum require different amounts of time.

## Frequently asked questions about Nieuw Amsterdam

### Where is Nieuw Amsterdam?

In Commewijne District, at the confluence of the Suriname and Commewijne rivers, relatively close to [Paramaribo](/suriname/place/paramaribo/).

### What is the main attraction?

The 18th-century Fort Nieuw Amsterdam, now used as an open-air museum. The riverside and boat excursions are also appealing.

### Is Nieuw Amsterdam the same city as New York?

No. The names have related historical origins but refer to different places. Nieuw Amsterdam in Suriname is a town and historic fort beside the Commewijne River.

### Does a tour that stops at the landing include the fort?

Not necessarily. A visit to the exhibitions and defensive works must be explicitly listed in the itinerary or arranged separately.

## Nieuw Amsterdam on Suriname tours

[Nieuw Amsterdam](/suriname/place/nieuw-amsterdam/) lies in Commewijne District, where the Suriname and Commewijne rivers meet. It is a convenient stop on trips around [Paramaribo](/suriname/place/paramaribo/), offering coastal scenery, history, and birdwatching.

Nieuw Amsterdam features on **three current Ada Tours itineraries**, but in different ways. On one, it is part of a dedicated birdwatching day; on two multi-country journeys, it is primarily a stop at the river landing after a visit to [Peperpot Nature Park](/suriname/place/peperpot-nature-park/). Seeing the town's name in an itinerary therefore does not guarantee the same attractions are included.

## Three itineraries and how they differ

| Tour | How the location is visited |
|---|---|
| [Birdwatching in Suriname, 8 days](/suriname/tour/suriname-birdwatching-8-days/) | Searching for coastal birds and owls, followed by a botanical garden |
| [Guianas Adventure, 9 days](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/) | River landing after Paramaribo and Peperpot, returning by boat |
| [Suriname, Guyana, French Guiana, 14 days](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/) | A combined day with Peperpot and a boat crossing |

**The birdwatching tour** is designed for travelers happy to start early and adjust the timetable to bird activity. **The multi-country itineraries** offer a broader journey, with Nieuw Amsterdam as one stop between historic Paramaribo, a former plantation, and the river.

In all these cases, the details of the specific day matter more than the number of territories in the tour's name.

## Nieuw Amsterdam for birds: a different experience

On the [eight-day birdwatching tour](/suriname/tour/suriname-birdwatching-8-days/), Nieuw Amsterdam is scheduled for day 7. In the morning, the group searches for owls and coastal birds in open areas by the water. Sightings depend on light, weather, tides, and the birds' behavior.

Afterward, the itinerary continues to the Cultuurtuin Botanical Garden in Paramaribo. The habitat changes from open coastal areas to the trees of an urban forest, where other bird species may be encountered. Specialist guiding and transfers are included in this particular birdwatching program.

If bird photography is your priority, the specialist itinerary offers more time to wait and observe than a quick stop en route to the landing. Compare other themed journeys in the [Suriname nature and wildlife tour catalog](/interests/wildlife/tours/suriname/).

## Nieuw Amsterdam on a journey through the three Guianas

On the [nine-day "Guianas Adventure"](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/), day three begins with a walk through historic Paramaribo. The route then continues through [Peperpot](/suriname/place/peperpot-nature-park/), a former coffee plantation gradually reclaimed by tropical vegetation. Travelers then arrive at the Nieuw Amsterdam jetty and return to the city by boat.

The [fourteen-day Guianas itinerary](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/) follows a similar sequence. On the boat section of the [Suriname River](/suriname/place/suriname-river/), it may be possible to see river dolphins, but sightings cannot be guaranteed.

It is important to distinguish **a stop at the jetty** from a detailed museum and fort visit. Nieuw Amsterdam does indeed have a historic fort associated with Commewijne's colonial past. However, these multi-country programs describe a boat transfer, so visits to the exhibitions and an extended walk around the fort must not be presented as included without agreement.

## Choosing history, nature, or a combination

If you want to learn more about former plantations and river geography, consider the combined Paramaribo–Peperpot–Nieuw Amsterdam day. It brings together wooden city architecture and Commewijne's landscapes. Dedicated early-morning excursions with specialist guiding are better for keen birdwatchers.

Anyone primarily interested in visiting the historic fort should confirm opening hours, tickets, and the possibility of spending extra time there. An extended museum visit cannot simply be inserted into an itinerary with a fixed boat departure.

We help arrange transport, the boat boarding point, and guiding options according to your chosen trip and interests. The full list is available in our [Suriname tour catalog](/suriname/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Nieuw Amsterdam

### Do all Nieuw Amsterdam tours include the fort?

No. Some only confirm a visit to the jetty and a return by boat. A museum visit needs to be allocated time and arranged separately.

### Which tour focuses most on birds?

The [eight-day birdwatching tour](/suriname/tour/suriname-birdwatching-8-days/) includes Nieuw Amsterdam specifically for observation, alongside other coastal and forest habitats.

### Can we see dolphins on the way back?

The Guianas programs mention this possibility on the river trip, but sightings of wild animals depend on conditions and are not guaranteed.

## Nieuw Aurora: a Saamaka village on the Upper Suriname River

Nieuw Aurora (also called Tutubuku) is a riverside village in the interior of [Suriname](/suriname/). It is a settlement of the Saamaka people, a Maroon group descended from Africans who escaped slavery in the colonial era and established independent communities deep in the forest. Travelers visit Nieuw Aurora to discover community life along a major tropical river.

Visitors do not come for a single building or museum. The village is a living community: people and goods arrive by river, there is a school, and residents go about their daily activities. A walk accompanied by a local guide offers an introduction to the village's history and how its cultural traditions continue today.

## Where is Nieuw Aurora, and how do you get there?

The village is on the Upper Suriname River, south of the usual urban routes from [Paramaribo](/suriname/place/paramaribo/). Travelers first drive to the river landing at Atjoni (also known as Pokigron), then continue in a motorized wooden boat known locally as a *korjaal*. The river replaces road access to most upstream settlements.

The boat journey passes forested banks and small communities. Travel time depends on the water level, current, departure point, and number of stops. This is an important part of the experience and a distinct logistical stage: you cannot plan the return to Paramaribo with the same assumptions as a trip along a paved road.

**Nieuw Aurora and Aurora are nearby but distinct settlements.** The name of neighboring Aurora appears on maps and in descriptions of the area; when choosing accommodation, a jetty, or an excursion, establish which village the boat will actually visit.

## What can you learn during a village visit?

### Daily life and community spaces

Our Nieuw Aurora itineraries mention a church, school building, medical post, and mission station. These are landmarks on a walk, not entertainment venues. Whether particular buildings can be visited depends on community rules and circumstances on the day; listing a site does not imply unrestricted entry.

Our ["Guianas Adventure" journey](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/) includes an introduction to the village and Maroon culture. The ["Suriname, Guyana, and French Guiana" route](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/) also includes Nieuw Aurora in its river section, with a walk and explanations of local plants.

### Saamaka history and culture

The Saamaka have their own language, community structures, and cultural practices. Their history is closely connected to resistance to slavery, the independence of forest settlements, and agreements reached with colonial authorities in the 18th century. Contemporary Saamaka people speak about their traditions for themselves: listening to a local guide is more informative than treating the village as a reconstruction of the past.

The forest and river remain part of livelihoods and daily life. Local people use plants in cooking, crafts, and traditional knowledge of nature. However, workshops, tastings, or dance performances can take place only as part of an agreed visit. On one of our programs, an evening cultural performance depends on a minimum group size, so it cannot be promised to every guest.

## How to behave on a cultural visit

A small-group visit with a local guide familiar with the community's visitor rules is the best approach. Ask before photographing people or homes. Buying locally made crafts and participating in cultural activities can support agreed forms of tourism, but residents themselves decide what they wish to share.

The community may have restrictions concerning access to particular areas, clothing, or photography; clarify them beforehand. Bring light closed-toe shoes, rain protection, water, and belongings that are easy to take aboard a boat. Comfort levels in river lodges may differ from a city hotel, and the specific itinerary determines accommodation and meals.

## How much time to allow and what to combine it with

Nieuw Aurora can be visited on an Upper Suriname itinerary, but reaching the village takes a substantial part of the trip. If you want to visit several villages, walk in the forest, and relax by the river, allocate more than a brief excursion slot to the region.

A river journey offers a very different experience from the historic districts of [Paramaribo](/suriname/place/paramaribo/) or walks through former plantations. [Bakkie Plantation](/suriname/place/bakkie-plantation/), for example, tells the story of the colonial economy on the coastal lowlands, while Nieuw Aurora introduces Maroon life in the interior.

To compare current options, open our [Suriname tour catalog](/suriname/tour/) and look for trips that explicitly visit Nieuw Aurora, noting the duration of the river section and whether an overnight stay is included. A vague reference to "meeting the Maroons" is no substitute for a specific place and agreed visiting arrangements.

## Frequently asked questions about Nieuw Aurora

### Is Nieuw Aurora close to Paramaribo?

No. It is a village on the Upper Suriname River, normally reached by driving to Atjoni and then continuing by boat.

### Who are the Saamaka?

The Saamaka are a Maroon group in Suriname, descended from African communities established in the country's interior. They have their own language, history, and cultural traditions.

### Can I visit the village without taking a boat?

Regular tourist routes to Nieuw Aurora use boats. The specific transport arrangements depend on the itinerary and available connections.

### Does every visit include a dance performance?

No. Cultural activities are agreed separately with the community and depend, among other things, on the number of participants. Your tour description should specify exactly what is included.

## Tours through Nieuw Aurora: a village on the Upper Suriname River

[Nieuw Aurora](/suriname/place/nieuw-aurora/) is a village on the Upper Suriname River in the country's forested interior. Maroon communities live here, descendants of people who left plantations during the colonial era and founded independent settlements inland. Today, a river trip to this area offers a chance to learn about local life and culture through a guided village visit.

We include Nieuw Aurora on two current itineraries: the [nine-day "Guianas Adventure"](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/) and the [fourteen-day "Suriname, Guyana, and French Guiana" journey](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/). In both cases, the visit is part of an organized river section, not a short outing from Paramaribo.

## Getting to the village

Travel on the Upper Suriname differs from road journeys on the coast. First comes a road transfer to the river landing near [Atjoni](/suriname/place/atjoni/), followed by a trip in a local motorboat. The river becomes the route between villages, islands, and forested banks.

Water and weather conditions matter along the way. River levels affect how easily certain stretches can be navigated and how the trip is arranged. Road transport, the boat journey, and the return time must therefore be planned as one logistical undertaking rather than booked as unrelated segments.

After the river section, travelers are introduced to Nieuw Aurora and its forest surroundings. The itinerary includes guiding and explanations of local traditions. This is a living settlement, not a staged tourist attraction.

## What is included in the day devoted to Maroon culture?

On the [nine-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/), the village visit takes place on day 8. The walk includes local community facilities, among them a church, school, and medical post. A guide explains Maroon culture and traditions. The program then includes a walk featuring plants used by local residents and stories about the area.

The [fourteen-day option](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/) has a similar village day and continues the exploration of Suriname's interior: a separate stage in [Kabalebo](/suriname/place/kabalebo/) begins after the river section.

On both itineraries, the cultural dance performance requires **at least eight participants**. It therefore cannot be promised to every couple or small group. Availability of particular activities must be agreed before departure.

## How nine and fourteen days differ

| Itinerary | Main focus |
|---|---|
| [9 days through the Guianas](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/) | A compact introduction to three territories and a river-based cultural visit |
| [14 days through the Guianas](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/) | The same principal territories plus extra days in Kabalebo's forests |

Both itineraries connect Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana, but the longer version has a more extensive forest section after the village. It includes separate outings to natural attractions, such as [Kilo 3 Rapids](/suriname/place/kilo-3-rapids/).

Choose according to how much time you want on rivers and in forests: the shorter option suits a first overview of the Guianas, while the longer one is for travelers happy to make additional domestic transfers and spend several days in the rainforest.

## Respectful conduct during a village visit

Nieuw Aurora is a place where a local community lives its everyday life. Photographing residents, visiting homes, joining cultural activities, and learning about crafts require respect for community rules and permission from the people involved. Working with a local guide helps prevent misunderstandings.

Bring light clothing that covers the skin, waterproof protection for equipment, and protection against sun and insects. For the boat journey, allow for extended time beside the water and follow the guides' advice. Check accommodation and meal arrangements against your chosen tour; similar routes do not necessarily include identical services.

## What to clarify before choosing a tour

Compare how many days the river section takes, what accommodation is specified, which day includes the village visit, when the group returns to [Paramaribo](/suriname/place/paramaribo/), and whether further domestic flights follow.

We help coordinate the transfers, local guiding, and an appropriate cultural program. Travelers primarily interested in life on the Upper Suriname should focus on the quality and content of the river day rather than the formal number of countries in a tour's title.

## Frequently asked questions about Nieuw Aurora

### Can I get to Nieuw Aurora by ordinary car?

On confirmed Ada Tours itineraries, reaching this area includes a boat journey after the road transfer. The route cannot be completed entirely by car.

### Is a dance performance included on every tour?

The itineraries specify a minimum of eight participants. For smaller groups, the performance needs separate arrangements and is not guaranteed.

### What does the fourteen-day itinerary add compared with the nine-day tour?

After the village and river section, it includes extra days in the [Kabalebo](/suriname/place/kabalebo/) forests, including a visit to [Kilo 3](/suriname/place/kilo-3-rapids/).

## Noordwijkweg in Suriname: morning birdwatching

**Noordwijkweg** is a birdwatching stop near [Paramaribo](/suriname/place/paramaribo/). Forest edges, scrub, and secondary woodland here attract birds moving between thickets and open spaces. Unlike a long expedition deep into the rainforest, this excursion provides an introduction to the birds of [Suriname](/suriname/) not far from the capital.

The key to this stop is watching and listening carefully. Often, a bird is first detected by its call or by movement in the leaves, and only then spotted among the branches. Such walks require patience from ornithologists and photographers alike: what you see in a day may differ from published species lists.

## Why depart at dawn?

In the tropics, the early hours are good for observation: the air has yet to heat up and birds actively forage and call to one another. Our itinerary uses Noordwijkweg specifically as a **morning** nature stop. A guide helps identify calls, distinguish similar silhouettes, and find places to pause without disturbing the birds.

A forest edge offers views of both low canopies and open vegetation. Yet bird appearances cannot be predicted: rain, wind, season, and chance all change what may be seen. Walking through too quickly usually leaves less time for meaningful observation.

## Which birds might you look for?

One stated target of this birdwatching itinerary is the **Crimson-hooded Manakin** (*Pipra aureola*). Males stand out for bright red plumage on the head and upper body. Females and younger birds are less conspicuous, so size, outline, behavior, and calls become important for identification.

Surinamese bird guides also report this species at other sites around Paramaribo, including swampy forests. A sighting on any particular walk is not guaranteed. The purpose of the outing extends beyond one species: observe the whole available area and record birds encountered.

### Birdwatching without disturbing nature

Move in small groups, keep voices low, and maintain a respectful distance from feeding or resting birds. Do not push into dense vegetation solely for a photograph, disturb nests, or try to attract birds by shouting or playing loud recordings. A long telephoto lens helps for photography; binoculars help with observation.

## What to bring

Light clothing in neutral colors that covers the skin offers protection from insects and scratchy vegetation. Bring water, a hat, closed shoes, and insect repellent. Protect electronics and optics from sudden rain. A morning outing does not necessarily involve strenuous trekking, but trail conditions depend on weather and local access.

A simple checklist is useful for recording sightings. If a guide uses local bird names, ask for the scientific or accepted English name straight away, so the identification can be checked after the outing.

## Noordwijkweg and the Weg naar Zee coast in one day

After visiting forest edges, the route can continue to the [Weg naar Zee coast](/suriname/place/weg-naar-zee/). These are two different habitats. Noordwijkweg focuses on forest birds, whereas the ocean shore offers waders, mangroves, and muddy flats exposed at low tide.

This contrast between forest and coast makes the day rewarding: even if the colorful manakin is not seen, a tidal shoreline can yield a different list of species. When planning, consider not only dawn but also **the tides** later in the itinerary.

Explore our other nature-focused trips in the [Suriname tour catalog](/suriname/tour/). If your visit includes the capital, allow time for [historic Paramaribo](/suriname/place/paramaribo/) as well, to discover the country's cultural side.

## Frequently asked questions about Noordwijkweg

### Who is Noordwijkweg best for?

Travelers interested in birds and wildlife observation. Experienced birdwatchers may want to compile a species list; newcomers can learn to spot and identify birds in the field.

### Is the Crimson-hooded Manakin always visible?

No. The species occurs in Suriname, but sightings depend on location, weather, and bird activity.

### Is special preparation required?

No demanding athletic preparation is specified for an ordinary outing on accessible paths. Closed footwear, insect protection, water, and binoculars are useful.

### What can I combine the walk with?

The [Weg naar Zee coast](/suriname/place/weg-naar-zee/), where coastal birds can be seen, and a visit to [Paramaribo](/suriname/place/paramaribo/).
